name: Slack
description: Full Slack workspace integration — read channels, search messages, manage saved items, post messages, add reactions, and manage user groups. Equivalent to the korotovsky/slack-mcp-server feature set, via browser session auth.
author: flock

requires.description: Log into your Slack workspace via the dashboard browser session
requires.rationale: Many Slack workspaces block bot token installs — a saved browser session uses your existing login with no admin approval needed.

saved_list.reason: With include_messages it fans out: one API call per saved item to fetch the linked message text, and _slack_api paces every call by 3s — so cost scales with how many items the owner has saved, not with the request. Measured live at 37s on a small account and killed at the 30s default, which discarded output the script had already produced.

channels_list.reason: One conversations.list call, but paced 3s by _slack_api and a cold call first extracts tokens from the browser session (~20s), which alone approaches the 30s default. Not a fan-out, so it does not need saved_list's budget.

users_list.reason: Unfiltered this is a single users.list call, but _slack_api paces every call by 3s and a cold call first extracts tokens from the browser session (~20s), which on its own passes the 30s default. With a `users` filter it keeps paging until every requested id is found — users.list has no server-side id filter, so a wanted id may sit on any page — and max_pages caps that at 20 pages of ~4s each. 120s covers that capped worst case without needing conversations_unreads' fan-out budget.

conversations_unreads.reason: Fans out to one conversations.history call per unread channel (max_channels defaults to 50) and _slack_api paces EVERY call by 3s, so cost scales with how many channels are unread rather than with the request. Documented as inherently slow: 1-5+ minutes on a large workspace.

conversations_search_messages.reason: A single search.messages call, but paced 3s by _slack_api and slow to return at count=100 on a large workspace - enough to pass 30s without being a fan-out.
